title: Interdependent conditions for successful human–AI delegation
title_zh: 成功的人机委托的相互依赖条件
abstract: People increasingly rely on AI systems for consequential tasks, from clinical diagnosis to software development. The gains are real yet difficult to realize reliably. We identify four psychological and structural conditions for successful delegation: accurate human assessment of AI capabilities, calibrated AI uncertainty communication, sustained human monitoring capacity, and compatible task structure. Each condition is well-studied, yet we propose that they form an interdependent system in which each one's effectiveness depends on the state of the others. Because these dependencies are bidirectional, we suggest that they can compound over time into virtuous cycles or cascading degradation, and that improving any single condition can fail or shift the bottleneck. These dynamics should intensify as AI moves from advisory roles to autonomous agents.
abstract_zh: 人们越来越依赖 AI 系统来处理从临床诊断到软件开发等重要任务。收益是真实的，但难以可靠实现。我们确定了四项成功委托的心理与结构条件：人对 AI 能力的准确评估、AI 不确定性的精准沟通、持续的人类监控能力以及兼容的任务结构。每项条件都已得到充分研究，但我们提出，它们构成了一个相互依赖的系统，每一项的有效性都取决于其他条件的状态。由于这些依赖关系是双向的，它们可能随时间形成良性循环或级联恶化，且改进单一条件可能失败或转移瓶颈。随着 AI 从咨询角色转向自主代理，这些动态应会更加剧烈。
